newsitem.title: USA: UAW ratifies labor pact with GM's Saturn.
newsitem.headline: UAW ratifies labor pact with GM's Saturn.

text.p: United Auto Workers said Thursday UAW-represented workers at General Motors Corp's Saturn unit have ratified a new labor agreement.
The workers voted 72 percent to 28 percent to accept the pact, UAW said. The vote was conducted on December 17 and 18.
The agreement covers about 7,200 Saturn workers in Spring Hill, Tennessee, and about 100 in Troy, Michigan.

It includes a $2,000 lump sum payment for 1997, to be paid in 1996, and wage increases of three percent in 1998 and 1999. The pact also includes 49 paid holidays, a $0.30 per hour skilled trades allowance in 1998, improvements in the dental and prescription drug plans and significant increases in Life, Disability and Survivor Income insurance, UAW said.

UAW said the contract also includes a legal services plan in 1998, improvements to health insurance and both Saturn and GM pensions, as well as a tuition assistance program for children of UAW-Saturn members and retirees, and the retirees themselves.
